bead.title: Prevent object-storage log one-command segment collapse
bead.description: The 10M hybrid-async release evidence run for pqueue-d6453cdd was stopped after ~60 minutes because perf sampling showed the hot thread spending CPU in std::path::Components::next under pqueue_objectlog::segmented::walk_keys -> LocalFsBlobStore::list -> SegmentedObjectLog::recover_manifest, called from SegmentedObjectLog::current_epoch/seal during ComposedBackend claim/finalize. The release harness uses 500-member push/claim batches, so 10M members should be roughly 60k durable batch commands, not 10M per-member records. However the composed read-modify-write paths force-seal around claim/finalize, and the object-storage segmented log produced one command per segment at scale (mean_commands_per_segment=1.0 in current evidence). That granularity is unacceptable for object storage. Most traffic must be batched, and command append interfaces should encourage and, for object-storage profiles, require batch operation instead of silently accepting tiny per-operation segment writes. If a transactional use case truly requires per-operation ack/apply, use a different log implementation or a local batcher/checkpoint layer; do not write one tiny object-log segment per batch command. In scope: change the command append/group-commit interface and objectlog/hybrid-async storage design so high-volume release workloads append multiple commands per object-storage segment, or explicitly route high-churn transactional commands to a non-object-storage log while preserving recovery. Add guardrails/tests so object-storage append APIs cannot regress to one-command segments for normal data-plane traffic. Fix manifest hot-path listing exposed by the selected design only as needed to meet the acceptance criteria. Out of scope: weakening the 10M release performance gates or accepting one-command object-log segments as release evidence.
bead.acceptance:
1. Add or update focused tests proving the object-storage command append interface requires or strongly enforces batched operation for normal data-plane traffic: a multi-command release-like workload must produce object-storage output with mean_commands_per_segment > 1 and max_commands_per_segment > 1, or high-churn transactional commands must be routed to a non-object-storage log while object-storage segment density remains >1.
2. Add or update a guardrail test that fails if a normal object-storage data-plane path can force one command per segment without an explicit low-volume/control-path override.
3. PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=1000000 cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture passes with bars_met=true and objectlog_hybrid_mean_commands_per_segment > 1.
4. A capped 10M preflight command, PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=10000000 timeout 15m cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture, must not spend the majority of sampled CPU in recover_manifest/walk_keys/current_epoch on the hot path; if it times out, capture perf evidence proving the dominant bottleneck moved away from manifest listing and leave pqueue-d6453cdd open. If it completes, bars_met must be true.
5. cargo fmt --check passes.
